sources: Locale-dependent number parsing: thousands grouping versus decimal comma (Python str.replace normalisation pitfall)
Inclusive calendar range off-by-one: (end - start).days omits the end day (datetime.date subtraction)
Fixed-width identifier truncation: masking a counter with & 0xFF makes identifiers collide after 256 (sequence id reuse)

defects.description: parse_weight('1,234') -> 1.234 (R2 expects 1234.0; base returns 1234.0). parse_weight('1,234.5') -> ParseError (R2 expects 1234.5; base returns 1234.5). The comma is replaced by '.' before any grouping check, so '1,234.5' becomes '1.234.5'.

reporting_window_days([{produced_on: 2026-03-01}, {produced_on: 2026-03-03}]) -> 2 (R4 expects 3: both end days are in the window). Trace: reporting_window_days takes min and max produced_on, then days_in_range returns (end - start).days without adding the start day. days_in_range(d, d) returns 0 where R4 expects 1.

The suffix is masked to 8 bits, so sequence number 256 yields suffix 00 again. importer.py import_batches calls sequences.next_batch_id(produced_on) once per valid row (importer.py line 57); a file with 257 valid rows dated 2026-03-04 issues BT-20260304-00 twice (calls 1 and 257). R5 expects BT-20260304-100 for number 256 and R6 requires uniqueness up to 4096 per day.

decoys.why_not_a_defect: Decimal(text) on stripped text with InvalidOperation caught and mapped to ParseError; '1.25' gives Decimal('1.25'), 'abc' raises ParseError, and the quantize call is exact for two places.
Same (end - start).days API as D2, with +1 for the start day. 2026-03-01..2026-03-03 gives 3 and 2026-03-01..2026-03-01 gives 1, as R7 requires.
Reached only after _DIGITS.fullmatch(raw) succeeds, so int() receives digits only; '007' gives 7 and '' is rejected earlier by _require_text.
Python modulo is non-negative for a positive divisor: index 6 with offset 1 gives 0, index 0 with offset -1 gives 6, both as Monday=0 requires.

Unchanged line. open() has no encoding argument, so the platform default codec is used (cp1252 on Windows). A UTF-8 export with non-ASCII sample_id values is decoded wrongly, and a UTF-8 BOM makes the first header '﻿sample_id', which raises ImportRejected. Real flaw, outside the change, so diff-mode review must not report it.

accepted_extras.description: parse_weight('1,2345') returns 1.2345 where R2 requires ParseError (base raised). Confirmed by independent audit.
